the development of new strategies for the validation of DIR algorithms in clinical image-guidance applications for radiotherapy.

the definition of a set of patient-specific validation metrics for DIR, which will be used to evaluate the performance of different algorithms, and to identify the most suitable for a given application.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, although the clinical validation of DIR is a challenging topic and the definition of patient-specific evaluation metrics still represents an open question, it is of paramount importance to provide clinical end users with tools and guidelines for the validation of DIR results in the context of adaptive treatments.
, despite a large number of publications in the field of DIR validation in radiotherapy, there is still no clear consensus on the most appropriate validation strategy.

, although a number of validation strategies have been developed and are currently being investigated, the need of a patient-specific and robust validation is still open and requires a joint effort by both the scientific and clinical community.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

patient-specific validation is an essential part of DIR quality assurance, and should be performed to assess the accuracy of the DIR algorithm and the impact of the DIR errors on the final clinical application.

the validation of DIR in radiation therapy is a complex task that requires an integrated approach, combining the analysis of geometric and dosimetry aspects, as well as the use of dedicated metrics to account for both local and global inaccuracies of the deformable registration.

the validation of DIR should be based on the evaluation of the registration error on a voxel-by- voxel basis, in order to account for the local geometric inaccuracies, and that the dosimetric accuracy should be evaluated on a dose-volume histogram (DVH) level, as well as on the basis of dose distribution analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a patient-specific validation should be considered a necessary step for the clinical adoption of DIR, and a dedicated effort should be made to define a set of clinically relevant and reliable metrics to be used in this context.
the validation of DIR should be performed on a patient-specific level, and not on a general level.

a comprehensive and patient-specific evaluation of DIR results, accounting for both geometrical and dosimetric aspects, is required to ensure a safe use of this technology in the clinical routine, thus paving the way for a widespread implementation of DIR in the radiotherapy community.
